## Summary

Discovered while fixing bug `unhelping-creviced-rhino` (`e127-a3ad-895a-4a2f`), which extended the
JS-safe decimal-string wire form from the MCP surface to CLI `--output json`. The NDJSON export
surface — `rebar export` and its library twin `rebar.export_tickets()` /
`rebar.iter_export_states()` (`src/rebar/_io/export_ndjson.py:168`) — was deliberately left OUT of
that change's scope and still emits bare 19-digit JSON integers.

## Evidence (measured, structural)

Against a freshly created ticket with a comment and a signature, using the e127 build (every other
CLI `--output json` surface reads 0):

```
show   --output json   unsafe ints: 0
list   --output json   unsafe ints: 0
audit show --output json unsafe ints: 0
export                 unsafe ints: 4
    $.created_at
    $.comments[0].timestamp
    $.signature.signed_at
    $.updated_at
```

RFC 8259 §6 guarantees numeric agreement only inside `[-(2**53)+1, (2**53)-1]`, so any float64
consumer of the export (jq, node, DuckDB/pandas via a JS-based loader) silently rounds these — the
same hazard e127 documents with a runtime-proven `node` reproduction (stored `…898642` reads back
as `…898600`).

## Why it was excluded from e127

Export is NOT `--output json`. It is a separately versioned interop projection carrying its own
`EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION` and a round-trip contract against `rebar import`
(`src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py`). Retyping the export side without a coordinated import-side
coercion would break `export | import` round-trips, so it needs its own change and its own
schema-version decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Decide the policy for the NDJSON export/import pair: adopt the same decimal-string wire form
      on export WITH matching `int()` coercion on import, or keep integers and document the hazard.
      → Adopted the decimal-string wire form: export emits via `js_safe_dumps`
      (`src/rebar/_io/export_ndjson.py:175`); import coerces `created_at`/`comments[].timestamp`
      provenance with `int()` via new `_coerce_ns` (`src/rebar/_io/_provenance.py`). Merged in
      `origin/main` `36ae045f41c3`.
- [x] If the representation changes, `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped and the change is recorded
      as BREAKING in `docs/release-notes.md` + `CHANGELOG.md` (per `docs/api-stability.md`).
      → `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1→2; BREAKING entries in `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/release-notes.md`,
      and `docs/import-export.md`.
- [x] A round-trip regression test proving `export | import` preserves the EXACT nanosecond digits
      (not merely the type) — a float64 round-trip gives `…600` for `…642`, so a type-only
      assertion would pass against a broken implementation.
      → `tests/interfaces/io/test_export_ndjson_js_safe.py::test_export_import_round_trip_preserves_exact_ns`
      (digit-exact) + `test_export_timestamps_round_trip_exactly`.
- [x] Structural coverage pinning whichever behaviour is chosen so the surface cannot drift.
      → `tests/interfaces/io/test_export_ndjson_js_safe.py::test_export_emits_no_uninteroperable_integer`
      fails on any bare >2^53 number on the wire (proven via sandboxed mutation: bare `json.dumps`
      → RED).
